design.mapHighlights:
dd-land-4 | route | Thevenot 1673 map: animate a glowing path up the Illinois and Des Plaines rivers to the Lac de Michigami shore, dropping a pulsing pin at the portage / site-of-Chicago where Jolliet and Marquette stood.
dd-land-6 | route | Knight & Zeuch portage survey: highlight the seven-mile portage corridor between the Des Plaines River and the South Branch, shade the Mud Lake basin, animate a canoe-path line across it.
dd-land-7 | region | Royce Illinois cessions map: highlight the northeastern Chicago-region cession polygon and draw an animated 20-mile-wide band from the lake toward the Illinois River as the 1816 St. Louis cession strip.
dd-land-11 | region | Van Vechten 1861 Cook County plat. s2 use: animate the diagonal Indian Boundary Line cutting across the township grid. s6 use: instead pulse the Hyde Park / Lake township block south of the city and the lakefront for the 'remade again and again' closer. Two distinct highlight treatments on the same plate. If strict single-use is required, swap the s6 instance for a fresh map land-cook-county-1853-plat (query: '1853 Rees map Cook County Hyde Park plat').

design.notes:
Beat-distinctness: every img/map/clip ref is unique across the whole film. The old cut repeated ~24 images 3x; this plan spreads ~63 beats across 24 existing land/formation assets (each once), 4 drone clips (each once), 1 pano, plus 27 fresh sources and 2 in-film quote cards. dd-land-11 is the only deliberate double-use (two different animated highlights in s2 and s6); a swap map (land-cook-county-1853-plat) is specified if strict single-use is enforced.

Maps are the variety engine. Six animated maps are spaced so no two map beats sit adjacent: dd-land-4 and dd-land-6 in s1, dd-land-7 and dd-land-11 in s2, land-blackhawk-warmap in s3, land-trail-of-death-map and dd-formation-7 in s5/s6. Let each map breathe 4-6s so the highlight animation reads; cut portraits and documents faster (1.5-2.5s) to build rhythm against the slow map reveals.

Pacing arc: s1 opens slow and atmospheric (drone reveal, pano, savanna/prairie/wampum stills) to establish the land as inhabited and whole BEFORE any deed. s2-s4 accelerate into a document-and-portrait cadence (Whistler, the sandbar survey, the 1812 battle, council scenes, treaty pages) so the 'land changed hands on paper first' theme is carried visually by maps and manuscripts. s5 is the emotional low (Trail of Death): hold the bronze marker and the Petit quote card longer and quieter, then turn upward on Shabbona-returned and the Pokagon portrait ('still here'). s6 resolves with three of the four drone clips bracketing historical stills, tying 1853 to today.

Drone clips: lakefront-reveal opens the whole film (s1); old-new-pan opens s6; greystone-rise mid-s6 on the 'sand ridges with bur oaks' callback; cornell-stone on the closing deed line. The script's 'ic-tracks' clip is not in the available clip set, so that beat was reassigned to cornell-stone; the script's duplicate lakefront-reveal beats in s1 and s6 were de-duplicated by pulling in the new savanna/prairie stills and greystone-rise.

Quote cards: two designed in-film typographic cards (Caton in s4, Petit in s5) replace the missing PD portraits the asset audit flagged (need-petit-portrait, need-1835-procession). Keep them visually distinct from each other (different rule/ornament) so they don't read as a repeated template.

Sourcing honesty: land-petit-quote-card and land-caton-quote-card are NOT Commons images (built in editor). land-river-sandbar-survey, land-trail-of-death-map, land-blackhawk-warmap, and land-sauk-trail-marker are the highest-risk to source (the audit found no clean PD hit for the sandbar survey, the Sauk Trail, and the 1835 procession). If any cannot be cleanly licensed, fall back to an in-film map graphic rather than substituting an off-period image. Verify the Whistler and Caton portraits resolve to genuine PD Commons files before locking.

critique.reuseFound: One ref repeats: dd-land-11 (the Van Vechten 1861 Cook County plat) is used in s2/map AND s6/map. All 44 img refs, both pano/clip groups, and the remaining map refs are otherwise unique (no img/pano/clip ref appears twice). The plan SELF-FLAGS the dd-land-11 reuse and offers two readings: (a) treat the two uses as distinct animated treatments on the same plate (Indian Boundary Line in s2; Hyde Park/Lake township pulse in s6), or (b) if strict single-use is enforced, swap the s6 instance for a fresh map "land-cook-county-1853-plat" (1853 Rees map). Under the stated test ("NO image/clip ref appears more than once"), a map plate counts as an image ref, so the s6 reuse FAILS strict single-use. Take fallback (b): make s6's closer "land-cook-county-1853-plat" (Rees & Rucker 1853 Cook County map, PD, easily found) and keep dd-land-11 solely for the s2 boundary-line beat. That also reads better, since the s6 "remade again and again" closer wants the township/lakefront subdivision plat, not the same boundary-line plate the audience just saw.
critique.coverageGaps:
Coverage is dense and mostly fitting, but several beats lean on generic stand-ins or near-duplicate scenery:
1. STAND-IN STACKING in s3-s4. land-illinois-militia ("1830s frontier militia"), land-army-column ("US Army column marching"), and land-removal-act-1830 ("Removal Act doc / Jackson portrait") are three back-to-back generic placeholders. land-army-column in particular illustrates an abstract narration line ("the army had proven it could be done") with no specific subject; consider replacing it with a stat card (badAxeSurvivors echo) or a map beat rather than a generic marching engraving.
2. SCENERY DUPLICATION. s1 opens with land-presettlement-oak (bur oaks) + land-prairie-wildflower (swale wildflowers) + pano-founding (grassland to horizon). s6 then reprises the SAME landscape twice: clip greystone-rise is described "Sand ridges with bur oaks, swales of wildflowers, prairie to the horizon" (a near-verbatim restatement of the s1 trio) and old-new-pan is generic. These are different ref ids so they pass the reuse test, but visually the film shows the same prairie-oak-swale image four-plus times. The greystone-rise clip is also misnamed (a greystone is a Chicago rowhouse, not a prairie) so the id fights its own description. Rename and re-shoot it as an actual old-to-new dissolve, or cut one of the s6 prairie beats.
3. WEAK/ABSTRACT QUOTE CARDS. land-caton-quote-card and land-petit-quote-card are in-film typographic cards, fine, but petit's card is justified by "no PD portrait exists," which is FALSE (see sourceability) — a George Winter portrait of Petit exists, so that beat can be a real portrait instead of a text card.
4. land-treaty-schools-clause asks for "a DIFFERENT manuscript page of the 1833 treaty" than land-treaty-chicago. Two near-identical scans of treaty text pages back-to-back (s4) read as one beat, not two; the schools/annuity clause is better served by a stat card (cashPromised/lastDancers already cover the numbers) or the McKenney-Hall council print. Risk of a flat "two pages of old handwriting" stretch.
5. dd-land-3 ("built Fort Dearborn at the mouth of the river") and land-river-sandbar-survey sit adjacent in s2 and both depict the same river-mouth geography; acceptable but watch for redundancy with land-early-chicago right after.
critique.sourceability:
Flags, riskiest first:
1. land-whistler-portrait — HIGH RISK, likely does NOT exist. No verified PD portrait of Captain John Whistler is on Commons; searches surface only James McNeill Whistler (the painter) and "Whistler's Mother," a real mis-sourcing trap. FALLBACK: drop the portrait and use a Fort Dearborn image instead (File:Fort Dearborn 1808.jpg and File:Birds eye view of first Fort Dearborn.jpg are on Commons and PD), or fold this beat into dd-land-3. Do not let an editor grab a James McNeill Whistler work by name match.
2. land-petit-quote-card — the rationale "no PD portrait exists" is WRONG. George Winter (1837-38) painted Father Benjamin Petit; Winter died 1876 so the work is PD. UPGRADE: source the George Winter Petit portrait (Tippecanoe County Historical Association / search "George Winter Benjamin Petit") and keep the quote card only if you want both.
3. land-1833-council / land-treaty-chicago — "Catlin or McKenney council scene" is plausible but there is no Catlin painting OF the 1833 Chicago treaty specifically. Use McKenney & Hall "History of the Indian Tribes of North America" Potawatomi plates (PD) or a generic PD treaty-council engraving, and label it as representative, not as the 1833 event.
4. land-agency-house — "1830s illustration of Wolf Point / the agency house" is borderline. The well-known PD image is the "Wolf Point, Chicago, 1833" view; search "Wolf Point Chicago 1833" rather than "Indian agency house," which may return nothing.
5. land-michilimackinac — fine as a concept but be specific: use a PD 18th-c map of the Straits of Mackinac or the known "Fort Michilimackinac" engraving; the generic query risks a modern photo.
6. land-sauk-village — Karl Bodmer's Sauk/Fox village views and George Catlin Sauk paintings exist and are PD; use those named sources rather than a generic "Saukenuk" query, which has no single canonical image.
7. land-removal-act-1830 — the document facsimile is obscure as an image; the safe PD pick is an Andrew Jackson portrait (abundant on Commons). Default to Jackson, not the act page.
8. land-presettlement-oak / land-prairie-wildflower — these will resolve to MODERN CC photos of Illinois prairie preserves (e.g. Nachusa, Midewin), which is fine, but they are CC-photo (attribution) not PD; confirm the license tier matches the film's needs.
9. land-blackhawk-warmap, land-trail-of-death-map — as static PD plates these are obscure; the plan already routes both through mapHighlights (animated route builds), which is the right call. Build them, don't source them.
10. land-watson-tavern, land-illinois-militia, land-army-column — generic-stand-in queries; PD engravings of frontier taverns and militia exist but are non-specific. Acceptable as mood, but tag them clearly as representative so no one reads them as the literal Watson tavern / specific militia.
Solid, low-risk sources: land-jolliet-portrait, land-marquette-portrait, land-caton-portrait (John Dean Caton), land-panic-1837 (E.W. Clay "The Times" 1837 lithograph), land-shabbona (Shabbona has known PD photos), dd-land-10/Pokagon — all plausibly on Commons as PD.
critique.verdict:
Close, but not yet clean. Three fixes are required before sourcing and assembly:
1. REUSE: resolve dd-land-11. Under a strict single-use test the s6 reuse fails; adopt the plan's own fallback and make the s6 closer a fresh "land-cook-county-1853-plat" (1853 Rees map), reserving dd-land-11 for the s2 Indian Boundary Line beat. This is also the stronger creative choice.
2. SOURCEABILITY: kill land-whistler-portrait (no PD portrait exists; James McNeill Whistler is a mis-source trap) and replace with a Commons Fort Dearborn view. Flip land-petit-quote-card to a real George Winter Petit portrait (the "no portrait exists" premise is false). Pin named PD sources for land-1833-council (McKenney & Hall), land-agency-house ("Wolf Point 1833"), land-sauk-village (Bodmer/Catlin), and default land-removal-act-1830 to an Andrew Jackson portrait.
3. COVERAGE: de-duplicate the prairie scenery (s1 trio vs s6 greystone-rise/old-new-pan — rename the mislabeled "greystone-rise" clip, which describes prairie but means a rowhouse, and cut one redundant landscape beat), and break up the two adjacent treaty-text scans in s4 (collapse land-treaty-schools-clause into a stat or council print). Trim the three back-to-back generic stand-ins in s3-s4 (militia/army-column/removal-act) to at most one.
With those three passes the plan is ready to source and assemble; everything else (Jolliet, Marquette, Caton, Panic of 1837, the animated map routes via mapHighlights, the Pokagon/Shabbona beats) is sound and well matched.
